title: Real Effects of Tax Uncertainty: Evidence from Firm Capital Investments
eligible_reason: Schedule UTP is phased in by firm size (assets >= $100M in 2010, >= $50M in 2012, >= $10M in 2014), so post_utp switches on at firm-specific years, but every reported regression includes about 18 standardized time-varying firm controls (cash ETR, cash flow, sales growth, Q, return volatility, leverage, size, KZ index, NOL, loss, working capital, acquisitions, R&D, managerial-ability rank, MNC indicator, etc.). The main sample (utp_firm==1) contains only eventually-treated firms; the columns that add never-UTP firms recode post_utp = 1 after 2009 for them and identify the effect from a second interaction term. No eligible specification. The package also contains no data (Compustat/CRSP via WRDS).
design_notes: SAS (I_consolidated_sasfile_Mar2021.sas builds the panel from WRDS Compustat fundamentals/segments, CRSP, plus managerial-ability, Loughran-McDonald constraint and EPU files) then Stata (stata_consolidated_03032021.do). Treatment: meets_utp_req = 1 if tax_form_year 2010-2011 & at >= 100, 2012-2013 & at >= 50, 2014-2015 & at >= 10; post_utp = 1 once cumulative_utp_req_yrs > 0 (absorbing). Table 3 (main): reghdfe spell_length_ma post_utp [18 controls] mnc if utp_firm==1 & utp_prim_diffindiff_sample==1, cluster(gvkey1) a(cyear gvkey1); N = 23,841 firm-years, 3,217 firms, 10 calendar years (2005-2014); coefficient on post_utp 0.371 (SE 0.118). Col 2 restricts to utb_at_hms != 0 (0.395, SE 0.128). Cols 3-4 add never-UTP firms with post_utp = 1 for cyear > 2009 and post_utpXutp_firm as the DiD term (col 4 uses sic2 x year-style FE: a(cyear sic2_firm_numeric)). Outcome spell_length_ma = _t from stset, the running length of the spell since the last investment spike (linear 'spell length' regression following Whited). Tables 4-5: subsample splits and interactions; Table 6: cash holdings with many controls; Table 7: investment level, R&D, acquisitions, employment with controls; Table 8: streg exponential/Weibull hazard models (nonlinear); Figure A.2: lead test f.post_utp..f4.post_utp; Table A.3: breakdown by initial treatment year (c.post_utp#c.post_2010 ... post_2014).
estimators_reported: reghdfe TWFE static with time-varying controls (firm + calendar-year FE, clustered by firm)
lead/lag TWFE with controls (Figure A.2, Table A.3)
n_adoption_cohorts: 3 scheduled cohorts (2010, 2012, 2014) plus firms crossing thresholds in 2011, 2013, 2015

ineligible_specs.reason: about 18 standardized time-varying firm controls plus mnc; sample restricted to eventually-treated firms
two treatment indicators (post_utp recoded to a 2009 post dummy for never-UTP firms, plus post_utpXutp_firm); time-varying controls
subsample splits, interactions, placebo dates; all with time-varying controls

screener_notes: Package: ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2021.4072/replication_package_MS-ACC-19-02105/ contains only code and logs (SAS program, SAS log, Stata do-file, Stata .smcl log, README.txt). No data files: the SAS program reads Compustat/CRSP from WRDS (downloaded 5/4/2018) and three non-WRDS files; the Stata do-file expects master_sas_02232021.dta. Published coefficients can be read from stata_log_mar2021.smcl (e.g., Table 3 col 1 post_utp 0.3712, SE 0.1179, N 23,841). Earlier regression extraction truncated the control list; the log confirms all main regressions carry the full control vector.
